summary: Admissible radial solution disproves the forcing identity in the nonzero-flux application proof. Local correction preserves the decay estimates. Core full-space rigidity argument remains supported in inspected scope.

problems.title: Incorrect forcing after removal of nonzero flux

locations.anchor: Lemma4.2 Step4, equation(73) and displayed f

problems.claim: For u1=u-a, a=cx/|x|^n and p_a=-|a|^2/2, the extended u1 satisfies equation(73) with the displayed forcing.
problems.parameters: n=4 (or any n>=4), R=1, u=a=cx/|x|^n, p=p_a, any0<|c|<=epsilon; inspect |x|>3 where eta=1 and v=0.
assumptions_verified: u1=0 and all compact extension terms vanish outsideB3
problems.actual_result: Left side of(73)=0. Printed f=-2(a dot grad)a=2(n-1)c^2 x/r^(2n), nonzero. For n4 at x=(4,0,0,0), first component=3c^2/8192. The separately executed c=1/100 numerical sample gives3/81920000; the admissible counterexample is parametric and does not assume that the unknown smallness threshold exceeds1/100.
problems.impact: The main exterior-decay proof for general nonzero flux applies the whole-space construction to an incorrectly identified PDE. Zero-flux case and Theorem1.1 rigidity proof are not affected. Theorem1.3 itself is not disproved.
problems.correction: Add2 eta(a dot grad)a to the displayed f, or express the interaction as -eta[(u1 dot grad)a+(a dot grad)u1].
problems.repair_verification: Exact algebra verified. The extra term is O(c^2 r^(1-2n)), faster than required r^(-n-1) for n>=4, and smooth on cutoff support. Existing smallness and convolution bounds survive this local correction. No author adoption.

problems.title: Opposite sign conventions in the half-space energy identity and flux definition

locations.anchor: Equation(51), definition of h(R), and ensuing monotonicity

problems.claim: With the printed h=-integral(partial_r u dot u-|u|^2 u^r/2-pu^r), the annular Dirichlet energy is h(R2)-h(R1).
problems.check_type: Independent integration-by-parts calculation; local analytic test is not a theorem counterexample
problems.actual_result: Green's formula gives E=F(R2)-F(R1) with F=integral(partial_r u dot u-Hu^r); printed h=-F gives E=h(R1)-h(R2). Thus printed h should be decreasing. Exact local Couette calculation confirms the sign but is explicitly outside the theorem's global decay assumption.
problems.impact: Sign bookkeeping only: use F instead of h, or reverse the difference and monotonicity. Boundedness, Sobolev integrability, zero endpoint subsequences and the final vanishing deduction all survive.
problems.correction: Remove the leading minus in the h definition, or use E=h(R1)-h(R2) and decreasing h consistently.
problems.repair_verification: Independent Green identity and endpoint logic verified; no globally decaying nonzero solution claimed.

focused_checks.verification: Independently subtracted the two steady Navier--Stokes equations for u=u1+a and derived the missing +2(a dot grad)a term. For a=c x/r^n, div(a)=Delta(a)=0, (a dot grad)a=(1-n)c^2 x/r^(2n), and grad(-|a|^2/2)=-(a dot grad)a. Every n>=4, R=1 and arbitrarily small 0<|c|<=epsilon is admissible in Lemma 4.2. Outside B3 the cutoff and divergence-correction terms vanish; u1=0 gives zero left side but nonzero printed forcing. Exact arithmetic at n=4,x=4e1 yields 3c^2/8192. The amended force is O(c^2 r^(1-2n)), hence satisfies the required r^(-n-1) bound. Theorem 1.3's general-flux proof depends on this equation; the example itself satisfies its decay conclusion and does not refute it or Theorem 1.1.
focused_checks.counterevidence: Read the smallness quantifier, zero-flux reduction and the subsequent convolution/uniqueness bounds; the repair does not require an unverified numerical lower bound on epsilon.

focused_checks.verification: Independently integrated -Delta u+(u dot grad)u+grad p=0 against u on the half-annulus. The flat boundary vanishes under no-slip conditions and the energy equals F(R2)-F(R1), where F is the outward radial integral of partial_r u dot u-(|u|^2/2+p)u^r. Thus printed h=-F must satisfy the reversed difference and be decreasing. The local Couette diagnostic has energy b^2 pi^2(R2^4-R1^4)/4 and is correctly excluded as a counterexample to the global decay theorem. The bounded monotone function and endpoint subsequence argument survive the sign correction.
focused_checks.counterevidence: The source's no-slip part is dimension four only. No nonzero globally C/r-bounded solution is inferred from the local diagnostic.
